units.title: Congruency and the Geometry of Size
units.intro:
Congruent figures: same shape and size — one maps onto the other by isometries. Triangle tests: SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS (right-angle, hypotenuse, side). AAA is similar, not congruent (Grade 11 similarity). AAS is ASA in disguise if you know the angle sum.

Corresponding vertices must be named in order. Tick sides and arcs on the diagram before you write a test name. Size also means perimeter and area recipes you already have — congruence says those match automatically.

cards.title: Not a test: SSA
body: The ambiguous case — don’t claim congruence from two sides and a non-included angle unless the book treats a special right-triangle case (RHS).

cards.title: More notes
body: Write “△ABC ≅ △DEF” only when A↔D, B↔E, C↔F. Then AB=DE, angle B=angle E, and so on. Proofs: list three matching facts, name the test, then harvest more equal parts as “corresponding parts of congruent triangles.”

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Two triangles $$ABC$$ and $$DEF$$ are congruent under the correspondence $$A \\leftrightarrow D$$, $$B \\leftrightarrow E$$, and $$C \\leftrightarrow F$$. If $$AB = 2x + 3$$, $$DE = 3x - 1$$, and $$BC = 12$$, find the value of $$x$$.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify corresponding parts**
Since $$\Delta ABC \\cong \\Delta DEF$$ under the given correspondence, corresponding sides must be equal in length. Therefore:
$$AB = DE$$

**Step 2: Set up the equation**
Substitute the algebraic expressions for $$AB$$ and $$DE$$ into the equation:
$$2x + 3 = 3x - 1$$

**Step 3: Solve for $$x$$**
Subtract $$2x$$ from both sides:
$$3 = x - 1$$
Add $$1$$ to both sides:
$$x = 4$$

**Step 4: Final Result**
The value of $$x$$ is **$$4$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: A sector of a circle of radius $$6\\text{ cm}$$ has a central angle of $$120^{\\circ}$$. Find the area of the sector.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify the formula for the area of a sector**
The area $$A$$ of a sector with radius $$r$$ and central angle $$\theta$$ is:
$$A = \\frac{\\pi r^2 \\theta}{360^{\\circ}}$$

**Step 2: Substitute the known values**
Here, $$r = 6\\text{ cm}$$ and $$\theta = 120^{\\circ}$$:
$$A = \\frac{\\pi (6)^2 (120^{\\circ})}{360^{\\circ}}$$

**Step 3: Simplify the fractions**
Since $$\frac{120^{\\circ}}{360^{\\circ}} = \\frac{1}{3}$$:
$$A = \\pi \\times 36 \\times \\frac{1}{3}$$
$$A = 12\\pi\\text{ cm}^2$$

**Step 4: Final Result**
The area of the sector is **$$12\\pi\\text{ cm}^2$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Find the volume of a sphere of radius $$3\\text{ cm}$$.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify the formula for the volume of a sphere**
The volume $$V$$ of a sphere with radius $$r$$ is given by:
$$V = \\frac{4}{3}\\pi r^3$$

**Step 2: Substitute $$r = 3\\text{ cm}$$**
$$V = \\frac{4}{3}\\pi (3)^3$$
$$V = \\frac{4}{3}\\pi (27)$$

**Step 3: Simplify the expression**
$$V = 4\\pi \\times 9$$
$$V = 36\\pi\\text{ cm}^3$$

**Step 4: Final Result**
The volume of the sphere is **$$36\\pi\\text{ cm}^3$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: A right circular cylinder has a radius of $$7\\text{ cm}$$ and a height of $$10\\text{ cm}$$. Find its total surface area. (Take $$\\pi = \\frac{22}{7}$$)
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify the formula for total surface area of a cylinder**
The total surface area $$SA$$ of a cylinder is:
$$SA = 2\\pi rh + 2\\pi r^2 = 2\\pi r(h + r)$$

**Step 2: Substitute the given values**
Here, $$r = 7\\text{ cm}$$, $$h = 10\\text{ cm}$$, and $$\pi = \\frac{22}{7}$$:
$$SA = 2 \\times \\frac{22}{7} \\times 7 \\times (10 + 7)$$

**Step 3: Simplify the expression**
$$SA = 24 \\times \\frac{22}{7} \\times 7 \\times 17$$
$$SA = 44 \\times 17$$
$$SA = 748\\text{ cm}^2$$

**Step 4: Final Result**
The total surface area of the cylinder is **$$748\\text{ cm}^2$$**.
